messages:
Alex M: quick question — is everyone ok with us pushing a pluggable burst-credit adapter instead of adding another hard reservation path?
Priya S: depends what we mean by pluggable. do you mean a shippable interface that can
swap implementations (credits, soft-reserve, prepaid) per-tenant at runtime?
Alex M: yeah. an adapter layer between the scheduling front-end and token accounting.
Jordan: pros i see: avoids adding N new code paths in the allocator, keeps admission logic
centralized, easier to A/B different credit schemes. cons: adds an indirection and a
potential performance hop for the fast-path.
Sam (infra): performance hop is small if we inline adapters and use a lightweight trait.
But the real question is correctness: can an adapter guarantee eviction semantics the
allocator needs? e.g., when we reclaim burst credits mid-request.
Priya S: also worth calling out billing/telemetry alignment. adapters will need to emit
the same signals so Optimize/Console don't explode. we can't have separate metrics models.
Tayla (sre): from an SRE perspective hard reservations are simpler to reason about for SLOs.
If a tenant holds X reserved GPUs, we can attribute latency regressions. credits are fuzzy.
Alex M: true. but hard reservations increase fragmentation and footprint. Customers asked for
a cheaper burst mechanism that doesn't require long-term commits. that's why credits exist.
Jordan: proposal: implement a pluggable adapter with a contract that MUST expose:
  * admit(request) -> admission_token
  * charge(admission_token, usage)
  * cancel(admission_token)
  * introspect(tenant) -> current_balance/reserved_quota
Adapter implementations can either be virtualized hard-reserve (pre-allocated tokens) or a
burst-credit algorithm. allocator only calls admit/charge/cancel and trusts the token semantics.
Sam (infra): that contract looks good. two followups: what about cross-tenant fairness?
If an adapter gives one tenant aggressive burst credits, operator needs visibility and limits.
Priya S: add an operator-facing policy layer: admin can bind an adapter per-pool and attach
guardrails (max-burst-per-tenant, global-burst-cap). adapter emits events for policy enforcement.
Tayla (sre): and we should make the built-in hard-reservation adapter offer strict SLA modes
(preempt-protection flags) so teams who care about tail latency can choose it.
Alex M: agree. timeline: we can prototype the adapter interface and one simple token-bucket
burst adapter in 2 sprints, plus a thin hard-reservation shim that uses same interface.
Jordan: testing plan: fuzz admission under node failure, simulate revoke mid-inflight, and
validate observability (per-admit/charge events indexed by tenant + request id).
Sam (infra): infra notes: adapters must be serializable in control-plane state so restarts don't
lose balances. prefer storing lightweight deltas, not full per-request history.
Priya S: action items:
  - Alex: sketch adapter API + proto defs (PR) by EOD Friday
  - Jordan: test harness scenarios for fuzz + preemption (start Mon)
  - Sam: design persistence schema for balances (RFC next week)
  - Tayla: define SLO templates for hard-reserve vs credit adapters
orch-bot: deploy-bot: added calendar event "Adapter design sync" for Monday 10:00am. :calendar:
Alex M: thanks all — leaning toward pluggable adapters with operator guardrails + a hard-reserve
shim. saves us from repeating allocator logic and keeps future schemes pluggable.
Tayla (sre): fine as long as we ship the SLO story and transparent metrics before GA.
Priya S: yep — telemetry spike is my biggest worry, we'll coordinate with Optimize to map fields.
Jordan: cool. i'll open the test plan issue and link Alex's API draft once it's up.
Sam (infra): i'll stub persistence and the admin policy hooks, rough PR next week.
Alex M: ok closing this thread for now, follow-ups in Monday sync. :thumbsup:
